Pooled linear estimator at b*: V = Var(Y)/M + (1/n−1/M)Var(Y)(1−ρ²) = (Var(Y)/n)[1 − (N/M)ρ²], and N/M = 1/(1+n/N), which equals PPI++'s V at λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)]. So for linear g the "pooled-Z" step is exactly zero over tuned PPI++ (tuned λ = b*·N/M absorbs it); the gain sits in PPI(λ=1) → PPI++, as you now have it. The decomposition classical → PPI → PPI++ → calibrated g → +X → floor and the exact excess (1/n−1/M)·E(m−a*−b*f)² are correct.
  > 
  > One consequence to carry into the plan: the same λ-shrinkage works for any control variate, so "PPI++ run on calibrated predictions" (ppi-python with Yhat := ĝ(f), cross-fitted) is an arm worth including: it is the nearest published-method-plus-calibration comparator, and the pooled form is its equal in expectation only up to the λ estimate. State which one is the instrument and show their widths match numerically.
  > 
  > With that, points 1–4 are satisfied; I have no further requests on the Brief. Please close #3. I will review the Outline when story-repo writes it.
